profiles.name: Joseph Boland
profiles.excerpt: Joseph Boland was a New York radio repertory actor whose surviving work is strongest in Words at War and early science fiction.
profiles.bio_html:
Joseph Boland worked in the New York radio repertory during the 1940s and 1950s. His credits place him in wartime literary drama as well as the emerging science-fiction anthologies of the postwar years.

Boland appeared repeatedly on Words at War and later on Dimension X and X Minus One, with an additional appearance on The Chase. The progression shows a performer moving from topical wartime material into speculative drama.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves six Words at War performances credited to Boland, two each on Dimension X and X Minus One, and one The Chase appearance.

profiles.name: Kay Stewart
profiles.excerpt: Kay Stewart was a versatile West Coast radio actress whose surviving work crosses literary anthology, detective drama, espionage and westerns.
profiles.bio_html:
Kay Stewart worked in the professional West Coast radio repertory during the postwar years. Her surviving cast record shows steady supporting work across several major network genres.

Stewart appeared on NBC University Theater, Rocky Fortune, Barrie Craig, Dangerous Assignment, Lux Radio Theatre and Tales of the Texas Rangers. That range reflects the flexibility expected of radio repertory performers.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves three NBC University Theater performances credited to Stewart, two Rocky Fortune appearances and additional work across detective, espionage, anthology and western programs.

profiles.name: Ken Williams
profiles.excerpt: Ken Williams was a New York radio repertory actor whose surviving work is concentrated in early science fiction and suspense.
profiles.bio_html:
Ken Williams worked across the New York radio repertory during the 1950s. His credits show repeated casting in science fiction as well as crime and dramatic anthology.

Williams appeared on 2000 Plus, X Minus One, The Chase, Rocky Fortune and Stroke of Fate. He also worked on other radio western and anthology programs beyond the current GRH holdings.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves four 2000 Plus performances credited to Williams, three X Minus One appearances, two The Chase broadcasts and additional work on Rocky Fortune and Stroke of Fate.

profiles.name: Loretta Young
profiles.excerpt: Loretta Young carried an Academy Award-winning film career into radio and then became one of early television’s most successful actress-producers and hosts.
profiles.bio_html:
Loretta Young was born Gretchen Michaela Young in Salt Lake City in 1913 and entered films as a child. She became a major Hollywood star and won the Academy Award for Best Actress for The Farmer's Daughter.

Young also worked extensively in radio adaptations before moving into television with The Loretta Young Show. She starred in, hosted and helped produce the anthology, becoming an important example of a woman exercising creative control over a prime-time television series.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves ten Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Young and one Screen Directors Playhouse appearance. Producing and hosting remain substantial second professions alongside acting.

profiles.name: Lou Horne
profiles.excerpt: Lou Horne was a later radio-drama repertory actor whose surviving GRH work is concentrated in Sears Radio Theater.
profiles.bio_html:
Lou Horne is best documented through the late-1970s repertory of Sears Radio Theater, one of the major attempts to sustain scripted radio drama after the classic network era.

Horne appeared in productions with veteran radio actors such as Parley Baer, Marvin Miller, Daws Butler and Elliott Lewis. The series moved among mystery, comedy and contemporary drama, requiring supporting players to shift roles from broadcast to broadcast.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 11 Sears Radio Theater performances credited to Horne, providing a focused record of his later radio dramatic work.

profiles.name: Mark Wing-Davey
profiles.excerpt: Mark Wing-Davey created the radio role of Zaphod Beeblebrox before becoming an award-winning stage director and teacher in Britain and the United States.
profiles.bio_html:
Mark Wing-Davey was born in London in 1948 and studied at Cambridge, where he became part of the university's theatre and comedy world.

He became widely known as Zaphod Beeblebrox in the original BBC radio and television versions of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. Wing-Davey later built a major career as a theatre director and teacher, including award-winning productions in New York and leadership in actor training.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 11 Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy performances featuring Wing-Davey as Zaphod. Directing remains a substantial second profession within his public profile.

profiles.name: Naomi Stevens
profiles.excerpt: Naomi Stevens began performing in radio as a child and developed into a prolific character actress across radio, film and television.
profiles.bio_html:
Naomi Stevens was born in Trenton, New Jersey in 1925 and entered entertainment while still a small child. Radio was among her earliest professional outlets, years before film and television made her a familiar character actress.

Stevens later became known for a wide range of ethnic and neighborhood character roles on screen while continuing voice and radio work. Her career ultimately included nearly a hundred film and television appearances.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves nine NBC University Theater performances credited to Stevens and two Sears Radio Theater appearances, documenting radio work from widely separated periods of her career.

profiles.name: Owen Jordan
profiles.excerpt: Owen Jordan was a New York radio repertory actor whose surviving work stretches from wartime anthology through science fiction to Theater Five.
profiles.bio_html:
Owen Jordan belonged to the New York radio repertory across several generations of dramatic broadcasting. His surviving credits place him in wartime, science-fiction and later anthology programs.

Jordan appeared on Words at War, Dimension X and X Minus One before becoming a recurring player on Theater Five during the 1960s. The span shows a performer who remained useful as network drama evolved.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves seven Theater Five performances credited to Jordan, two Words at War appearances and additional work on Dimension X and X Minus One.

profiles.name: Peter Retray
profiles.excerpt: Peter Retray was a recurring member of the Theater Five company during ABC’s weekday radio-drama revival of the mid-1960s.
profiles.bio_html:
Peter Retray is best documented through Theater Five, ABC's weekday anthology that attempted to restore regular network radio drama during the 1960s.

The program changed genre and character with every broadcast, so recurring actors had to establish new roles quickly inside tightly scripted half-hour stories. Retray's repeated casting places him firmly inside that working repertory.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 11 Theater Five performances credited to Retray, providing a concentrated record of his later network-radio work.

profiles.name: Rosalind Russell
profiles.excerpt: Rosalind Russell brought one of Hollywood’s great comic and dramatic screen careers to radio through prestige adaptations and star anthologies.
profiles.bio_html:
Rosalind Russell was born in Waterbury, Connecticut in 1907 and became one of Hollywood's most versatile leading actresses. Her screen career ranged from screwball comedy in His Girl Friday to dramatic and musical roles, earning multiple Academy Award nominations and a Tony Award.

Radio repeatedly invited Russell to recreate or adapt major screen and stage roles. She appeared on Screen Directors Playhouse, Lux Radio Theatre, Academy Award Theater and Screen Guild Theater, where her fast timing and strong characterization translated naturally to the microphone.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves five Screen Directors Playhouse performances credited to Russell, four Lux Radio Theatre appearances and additional broadcasts on Academy Award Theater and Screen Guild Theater.
